context.body: They came to Jericho. As he went out from Jericho with his disciples and a great multitude, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting by the road.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: A blind beggar hears Jesus is passing, cries “Son of David,” persists through rebuke, throws off his cloak, names his request, receives sight, and follows on the way.
observations.label: Bartimaeus calls Jesus Son of David: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Jesus, Bartimaeus, the crowd, and callers, Jericho’s roadside and the way, hearing, crying, rebuking, calling, throwing a cloak, asking, seeing, and following visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Bartimaeus calls Jesus Son of David: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Jesus, Bartimaeus, the crowd, and callers · Jericho’s roadside and the way · hearing, crying, rebuking, calling, throwing a cloak, asking, seeing, and following · Davidic address becomes a persistent plea and movement onto the way
observations.label: Relationships named in Mark 10:46–52

payload.posture: Read Mark 10:46–52 as its own gospel and apostolic memory David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places Davidic address becomes a persistent plea and movement onto the way inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: Bartimaeus calls Jesus Son of David
